review:
Absolutely NOT normal.

The intro is insanely long and boring. I kept waiting - okay, this is buildup, I'll be rewarded with something good.
Nope.

There are some messy, fun moments. A few jokes land. But it's all too rare. Instead, the movie keeps filling time with empty, placeholder scenes.

And then that plot twist... ridiculous. Completely stupid.
Like when the Yakuza suddenly show up in Minnesota - come on.

I could forgive dumb plot if the movie delivered energy.
If it was John Wick.
Or at least something fun and chaotic.

But it's neither.

Not funny enough.
Not stylish enough.
Just stupid.

Around 2/3 in, I already wanted to leave. Stayed only hoping they saved something for the ending.
They didn't.

Waste of time.

4/10
(and that's generous - only for a couple decent action/comedy moments)

I thought the cast was an interesting and eclectic bunch. Never seen a person use a nail as a toothpick before lol. Only a foreign person to the Midwest could write that one lol. review: A solid enough crime thriller, with a unique twist in the middle. The fault lies in the tone. This movie feels like it\s trying hard to have a quirky Fargo, indie type vibe, but doesn't pull it off. leaving a bit of a bland taste in my mouth. A temporary cop rolls into town to replace a dead sheriff until a new one is voted in. Everything seems normal in Normal, Minnesota, but at closer look, the town seems pretty wealth for a small town, and the police arsenal is stocked like they are guarding LA. The Townsfolk seem a bit too chipper too. This is where the filmmaker really could have capitalized on throwing in some offbeat characterization, which just wasn't the case. They chose Vanilla over Strawberry. The mandatory shoot out in the end was necessary and made sense without going all 'John Wick' which would not have fit for this. Bob Odenkirk, i thought was a bit miscast. His style was a bit too casual for all that was going around him. Overall, not bad, but not great.

review: Normal is anything but "normal".  It is the most outrageous, hilarious, incredible story/movie/adventure -- and sometimes bloodbath -- that anyone could imagine -- assuming anyone could imagine it -- as I am astounded by its uniqueness.  Normal is the story of a small town,  a replacement sheriff, and most of its inhabitants -- with a twist that will absolutely floor you.  Mayberry at its best -- with more twists than you can shake a stick at.  A sudden bank robbery upsets the local laid back sheriff's office -- and hold on to your seats -- because we're suddenly off into cinematic outer space where just about everything goes -- and does.  Anyway -- I don't want to spoil it for you.  I just have to say that it's a load of laughs -- from start to finish -- even the bloody parts.  (nothing like Kill Bill type - as all these actually somehow make sense).  Go see it.  Best comedy/action movie I've seen in years!!!!

name: Kevin R
review:
I went into Nobody as a longtime fan of Bob Odenkirk, expecting a fun, sharp action film with his signature offbeat charm. Unfortunately, what I got fell well short of that expectation.
To be clear, I wasn’t looking for a deeply layered character study—but I did expect a plot with at least some substance. Instead, the film leans heavily on stylized violence without giving the audience much reason to care about what’s happening. The story feels thin, almost like a vehicle designed solely to string together action sequences rather than tell a compelling narrative.
The humor, which should have been a strong point given Odenkirk’s background, rarely lands. It often feels forced, as if the film is trying to wink at the audience without earning those moments. What could have been clever or darkly funny instead comes across as flat and forgettable.
In the end, Nobody isn’t so much "normal" as it is disappointingly dull.
